html:
The Hafsids were a dynasty that ruled Tunisia and its neighbours from 1229 to 1574, with Tunis as their capital. They are the longest-ruling dynasty in Tunisian history.

They began as Almohad governors and broke away when the Almohads declined. Under them Tunis became the main city of the land, as it still is, with mosques, madrasas and markets around the Zaytuna mosque. They traded with Venice, Genoa and Aragon, and survived a French crusade under Louis IX, who died outside Tunis in 1270.

The historian Ibn Khaldun was born in Hafsid Tunis and served its court. In the 1500s Tunis was fought over by Spain and the Ottomans, who took it for good in 1574. See also the Hafsid state.
